expanded_name: Support-Preserving Adaptive Residual Kernel with In-domain Neighbour Gating
research_question: Does support-gating a nonlinear residual improve composition-only experimental band-gap prediction under preregistered element exclusion relative to the identical ungated residual model, without practically degrading official Matbench MAE?
hypothesis: A regularized linear component is safer for descriptor-space extrapolation, while nonlinear residual corrections are useful in-support but brittle out-of-support; attenuating only the residual as support distance increases will reduce leave-one-element-out MAE.
falsifier: The hypothesis is not supported if the confirmatory macro-MAE improvement over the ungated matched control is at most 0.01 eV, fewer than four of five element holdouts improve, or official five-fold MAE degrades by more than 0.02 eV.
intended_contribution: A small, auditable, compute-matched residual gate and a protocol that separates IID benchmark utility from element-exclusion extrapolation.

included: development element holdouts Cu, Ag, B
confirmatory element holdouts Li, Zn, Ga, Se, Te

predecessor.preservation_rule: Do not edit, replace, or reinterpret predecessor failure receipts.

claims.text: Support gating preserves official Matbench MAE within 0.02 eV.
